— you'd need to add Mailchimp or similar for email campaigns.

. It requires almost zero training since

.

## Why not the others for a 2-person firm

- **HubSpot** — the free tier is tempting, but the platform is built around scaling into marketing/service hubs you don't need yet, and

citations.cited_text: HubSpot works best when you have clear processes, consistent lead volume, and someone on the team who owns operations. For smaller consulting teams or...

content.text: it works best when you have clear processes, consistent lead volume, and someone on the team who owns operations — for smaller teams it can feel like more CRM than you really need

.
- **Pipedrive** — great for visualizing a sales pipeline, but

citations.cited_text: Where Pipedrive can fall short is after the deal closes. It’s built to help you win work, not necessarily manage long-term relationships, delivery con...
citations.title: Best CRMs for consultants and consulting firms in 2026 | Copper CRM

content.text: where it falls short is after the deal closes — it's built to help you win work, not necessarily manage long-term relationships, delivery context, or follow-on opportunities

, which matters a lot for a relationship-driven 2-person practice.
- **Zoho CRM** — cheap and flexible, but

citations.cited_text: The interface can feel dated, so expect some friction during setup.
citations.title: The 9 Best CRM Platforms for Consulting Firms in 2026 | SCG

content.text: the interface can feel dated, so expect some friction during setup

— overhead you don't want with no dedicated admin.
- **Insightly** — its real strength is merging CRM with project delivery, but that's

citations.cited_text: Insightly works well for mid-sized consulting firms that want CRM plus project management in one place.
citations.title: The 9 Best CRM Platforms for Consulting Firms in 2026 | SCG

citations.cited_text: The learning curve is steeper than simpler tools.
citations.title: The 9 Best CRM Platforms for Consulting Firms in 2026 | SCG

content.text: better suited to mid-sized consulting firms, and the learning curve is steeper than simpler tools

— more structure than two people typically need.

**Bottom line:** Start free on Capsule (or Copper if you're Gmail-native), and only graduate to something heavier like Insightly or HubSpot once you add consultants #3–5 and need real pipeline discipline or delivery tracking.
